llm.reply:
Lynch syndrome is characterized as a distinct disease entity across multiple NCBI databases [7]. It is linked to multiple mismatch repair and associated genes, including mutL homolog 1 [10]. Clinical trials evaluate testing, patient identification strategies, and risk registries [1].

## Associated Genes

The disorder is linked to the gene NCBIGene:4292 [10]. It is also associated with the mismatch repair factor mutS homolog 2 [11]. Further associated entities include mutS homolog 6 [8]. The related genes extend to PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component [14].

## Clinical Trials

Trial protocols include Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1]. Clinical research also comprises Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer in Taiwan-Related Genetic Study and Clinical Applications [2]. Patient support and testing perceptions were evaluated in Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3]. Tracking and surveillance studies include Registry for Women Who Are At Risk Or May Have Lynch Syndrome [5].

## Literature and Condition Records

The disorder corresponds to the record medgen title: Lynch syndrome [19]. Biomedical publications discuss screening and disease recognition under the title Identification of Lynch Syndrome [28]. The genetics and translational aspects are further detailed under the title Lynch Syndrome Genetics and Clinical Implications [30]. Related concepts in the literature encompass the entity name Lynch syndrome I (site-specific colonic cancer) [20].

The disease name is Lynch syndrome [7]. Across NCBI, associated loci include mutL homolog 3 [6], mutS homolog 6 [8], epithelial cell adhesion molecule [9], mutL homolog 1 [10], mutS homolog 2 [11], neurofibromin 1 [12], PMS1 homolog 1, mismatch repair system component [13], PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component [14], ribosomal protein S20 [15], transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 [16], and cadherin 1 [17].

## Clinical Trials

A clinical trial name is Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1]. Another clinical trial name is Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer in Taiwan-Related Genetic Study and Clinical Applications [2]. A related clinical trial name is Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3]. Educational interventions include the clinical trial name Educational CD-ROM Compared With Standard Informed Consent for Patients With Colorectal Cancer or a Family History of Colorectal Cancer [4]. In addition, registry efforts include the clinical trial name Registry for Women Who Are At Risk Or May Have Lynch Syndrome [5].

## Condition and Entity Records

The medgen title is Lynch syndrome [19]. A related literature entity name is Lynch syndrome I (site-specific colonic cancer) [20]. An additional literature entity name is Colorectal Neoplasms Hereditary Nonpolyposis [23]. Another literature entity name is Lynch Syndrome II [26].

## Associated Literature

A pubmed title is Lynch syndrome. [18]. A publication pmid is 21508689 [21]. A relevant pubmed title is Differentiating Lynch-like from Lynch syndrome. [22]. Another publication pmid is 24468183 [24]. A related pubmed title is Overview of Prostate Cancer Genetic Testing. [25]. A publication pmid is 34210484 [27]. An additional pubmed title is Identification of Lynch Syndrome. [28]. Another publication pmid is 34798986 [29]. Finally, a pubmed title is Lynch Syndrome Genetics and Clinical Implications. [30].
